non-pharmacological treatment in combination with drug one in patients with CCF of NYHA functional classes I-II consequent on myocardial infarctions is a promising way to reduce the risk of unfavorable outcomes of the disease.

The main takeaway from our work is that

in asymptomatic chronic cardiac failure consequent to myocardia infarction, the long-term combined therapy with nonpharmacological methods of treatment is a highly effective means of reducing the rate of LV remodelling, decreasing LV hypertrophy, improving LV systolic-diastoliic function, and lowering the cumulative risk of unfavorable outcomes of the CCF by 42%.
the nonpharmacological therapy of chronic cardiac failure after myocardial infarct is an important component of the complex treatment of the patients.
nonpharmacological therapy is a necessary component of the treatment of CCF, and the effect of this component is not less important than that of pharmacological therapy.
